title: Beatrix and the Tide
premise: Beatrix Fairweather, a celebrated cellist whose final performance ended in a collapsed memory and a shattered reputation, has spent two years hiding in her family's coastal inn, teaching children scales and avoiding the stage. When her grandmother's will demands every heir attend the summer reunion with a partner or forfeit their inheritance, Beatrix bribes Cyrus Hale—a lighthouse restorer who once played second cello beside her—to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake romance deepens through salt air and family secrets, until Beatrix discovers the reunion itself is a test: her grandmother's letters reveal the inheritance hinges on whether Beatrix will perform again, and Cyrus has known all along, hired by the family to coax her back. Betrayed, she nearly retreats into silence forever, but at the tide's lowest ebb she realizes loyalty to her own music matters more than the truth of how she was pushed toward it; she plays the piece that broke her, on the beach at dawn, and chooses both the career and the man who now earns forgiveness honestly.
about_author: Felix Underhill is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade cataloguing other people's crescendos before writing her own stories. She lives in a converted boathouse on the Maine coast, where she still cannot keep a houseplant alive but has never missed a high tide.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Two years after her catastrophic final performance, Beatrix teaches a nervous child a simple scale at her family's seaside inn and deflects a letter from a symphony asking if she'll ever play again. The emotional beat is quiet avoidance—she has built a life sized exactly to hide inside.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Her grandmother's lawyer arrives with the will: each heir must attend the August reunion accompanied by a committed partner, or their share passes to the others. Beatrix's scheming cousin Delia smirks, certain Beatrix will come alone. The beat is dread sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixed Lighthouses
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus Hale, restoring the inn's derelict lighthouse, recognizes Beatrix from their conservatory days when he sat second chair behind her. He remembers the performance no one else will mention. The beat is wary tenderness—he sees her clearly, which frightens them both.

chapters.title: A Transaction in Salt Air
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Over mended lobster traps and cheap wine, Beatrix offers Cyrus room, board, and his boat's engine repairs if he'll pose as her boyfriend for the reunion weekend. He agrees with unsettling ease. The beat is nervous exhilaration disguised as business.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They invent a courtship story on the inn's porch—first date, first fight, first song—and the invented details keep sounding true. Cyrus hesitates over one question about why he really left music. The beat is intimacy arriving faster than the fiction can hold.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The family descends: Delia with her perfect fiancé, estranged brother Marcus, and Aunt Wren who watches everything. Beatrix introduces Cyrus and feels the strange pride of presenting something real-shaped. The beat is performance anxiety without a stage.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the welcome dinner, Cyrus defends Beatrix against Delia's needling with a story about her courage that he improvises—and means. Under the table, their hands link. By dessert, the fake date has stopped feeling fake. The beat is falling, unwillingly.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Cyrus shows Beatrix the lighthouse lamp room at dusk and admits he quit the conservatory after watching her collapse on stage—it broke something in him too. She almost tells him what really happened that night. The beat is two people circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Searching the attic for table linens, Beatrix finds her grandmother's sealed letters—one per heir, to be opened at reunion's end. Hers is heavier than the others. She doesn't open it yet. The beat is foreboding wrapped in inheritance.

chapters.title: The Regatta Gambit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A family sailing race forces Beatrix and Cyrus onto one small boat; capsized and laughing in the shallows, they kiss for the first time with witnesses cheering. Delia's smile falters. The beat is joy so loud it drowns suspicion—for now.

chapters.title: Marcus's Warning
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Marcus corners Cyrus privately: he's seen this trick before, and asks what Cyrus is being paid. Cyrus lies badly. Marcus reveals the family suspects the 'boyfriend' was arranged. The beat is guilt tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: Interlude: Four Hands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Late at night, Cyrus coaxes Beatrix to the inn's neglected piano, and they play a duet badly and gloriously—her first music-making in years that doesn't hurt. She cries afterward and lets him stay. The beat is thawing, terrifying and sweet.

chapters.title: Delia's Discovery
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Delia confronts Beatrix with evidence: a check stub, a phone record—Cyrus was hired. But by whom, even Delia doesn't know. Beatrix's world tilts; she remembers how easily Cyrus agreed. The beat is betrayal's cold first draft.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Beatrix demands the truth. Cyrus confesses: Aunt Wren hired him months ago to get close, believing only trust could bring Beatrix back to music—but swears the love became real. Beatrix walks out into the storm. The beat is heartbreak with a splinter of doubt.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone on the exposed flats at low tide, Beatrix finally opens her grandmother's letter: it contains the program from the disastrous concert and a single line—'The music didn't fail you; the lie you told yourself did.' The beat is devastating clarity.

chapters.title: What Really Happened
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Flashback chapter: the night of the collapse, Beatrix played on a broken finger because her then-manager demanded it, then let the world blame her memory rather than admit she'd been exploited. The beat is reclaiming her own story from shame.

chapters.title: The Reunion Verdict
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the final dinner, the lawyer reads the will's condition: the inn and its endowment go to whichever heir demonstrates 'the courage of their calling.' Delia presents her gallery; Marcus his firm. All eyes turn to Beatrix. The beat is the trap closing—or the door opening.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Choice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Refusing Wren's final payment, Cyrus stands before the family and tells the whole truth—the hiring, the letters, and that he loves Beatrix regardless of outcome, then leaves the decision entirely to her. The beat is loyalty choosing truth at last.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Dawn, the beach, the borrowed cello from the inn's parlor. Before the assembled family and the rising tide, Beatrix plays the piece that broke her—shaky, then sure, then transcendent. The beat is catharsis; the silence ends.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The lawyer announces the inn goes jointly to all heirs as a working arts retreat—her grandmother's true design. Beatrix declines the solo share, keeping instead the lighthouse lease. The beat is inheritance redefined as purpose, not property.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Weeks later, Cyrus finishes the lighthouse restoration. Beatrix returns from her comeback audition—accepted—and finds him waiting with two tickets and an apology he already made. She asks him to stay not as an employee but as himself. The beat is forgiveness earned and given.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. One year later: the inn hosts its first summer concert series; Beatrix performs on the beach at high tide while children dance and Cyrus watches from the lamp room. Her grandmother's letter rests framed above the piano. The beat is full-circle peace—memory honored, truth kept, love chosen daily.
